notes: Clean, well-decomposed course: the large majority of flags are false positives — bare function words/particles (non, di, da, al, mi, ci, che, per, a, in, con) sub-glossed contextually inside larger LEGOs (53 fp_subgloss), plus English target morphology of one lemma (have/was/want/speak inflections, a/an) (26 fp_inflection). The two real, systemic, learner-facing issues are Italian intonation-questions ('parli X' = both 'you speak X' and 'do you speak X?', recurring 10x — needs the statement->question convergence) and gender-ambiguous 'suo' (his/her name, recurring 6x); fare (make vs do) is the only other genuine semantic overload.

real_fixes.known: parli (and the whole parli-family: parli?, parli inglese?, parli inglese tutto il giorno?, parli inglese molto bene, parli molto bene?, parli inglese con me?, parli un po' di inglese, parli inglese con qualcun altro, parli inglese dopo che finisci?)
targets: you speak English / do you speak English?
real_fixes.action: Systematic Italian intonation-question collision: identical 'parli X' maps to BOTH the English statement ('you speak X') and the do-question ('do you speak X?'). Pick ONE canonical surface per drilled item via the statement->question convergence (render declarative 'you speak X', let the question be the same prompt) so each Italian prompt has one English answer.
real_fixes.canonical_english: you speak X (declarative; do-question converges to same prompt)

real_fixes.known: il suo nome (+ imparare/voglio/vuoi ricordare/mi piacerebbe scoprire il suo nome)
real_fixes.action: Italian 'suo' is gender-ambiguous (his OR her). The identical drilled prompt maps to both 'his name' and 'her name', so the learner cannot know which to say. Differentiate the prompt (use possessor context, e.g. add the named referent) or fix the decomposition so each Italian prompt resolves to one English answer; recurs across ~6 seed pairs.

Single drilled verb 'fare' is glossed as both MAKE and DO (genuinely distinct intentions). Split: keep make-senses on phrases meaning produce/create and do-senses on phrases meaning perform/act, so each phrase's Italian context maps 1:1; or differentiate the prompt.
speak and talk are the same intention for 'parlare'; collapse to one English verb (speak) across drilled items.
Same quantity-intensifier intention; pick one canonical English for the drilled 'molto' (much) and re-gloss the others to it where it is the standalone prompt.
Same intention (like/enjoy); re-gloss to the drilled canonical 'I like'.
say/tell are the same intention for 'dire'; collapse to the drilled canonical 'say'.
'we need to' vs 'we must' are the same obligation intention; re-gloss to the drilled canonical.
job/work both render 'lavoro'; pick one canonical for the drilled noun and apply to the 'most important job/work' phrase too.
all/everything same intention; re-gloss to the drilled canonical 'everything' (component 'all' to match).
Same sentence intention (need to/must); pick one canonical surface.
'non c'era' = there wasn't; the bare 'wasn't' drops the existential 'there'. Consolidate to 'there wasn't'.

targets: are you not happy any more?
real_fixes.action: Statement vs question of identical Italian; converge to one canonical declarative surface.
it's/that's are meaning-equivalent renderings of 'è' here; pick one canonical.

targets: do you know what I mean?
real_fixes.action: Italian intonation-question collision (statement vs do-question of identical prompt); converge to one canonical surface.

targets: she didn't understand the question before
real_fixes.action: Identical Italian but one English adds 'before' (no 'prima' in the Italian); drop the spurious 'before' (or correct the known if it should contain 'prima').

real_fixes.known: È utile rispondere il prima possibile
targets: it's useful to answer as soon as you can
it's useful to answer as soon as I can
real_fixes.action: Italian 'il prima possibile' is impersonal ('as soon as possible'); injecting 'you can'/'I can' creates two answers for one prompt. Render the impersonal canonical so it maps 1:1.
real_fixes.canonical_english: it's useful to answer as soon as possible

targets: I'm not going to be able to speak
I won't be able to speak
real_fixes.action: going-to vs won't are the same future intention; pick one canonical surface.
real_fixes.canonical_english: I won't be able to speak
